description:
FILED s453 (Fable box-elision review, faster-codegen-suggestions.md par.13 gap 3).  nested-sub-ref boxes EVERY name captured by an anon sub, categorically.  Probe: a closure that only READS $s still boxes it.  CL closures capture let bindings natively (shared, mutable, kept alive), so a raw let slot works for capture-and-read AND capture-and-write; the box is needed only when a REAL boxing event exists (backslash-ref, local, string eval in region, aliasing) -- and the event walk already descends into nested sub bodies, so those fire on their own.  FIX: narrow the veto from capture to capture+event.  CARE: (a) named subs capturing block lexicals are the FILE-PROMOTION story (p-defcell) -- out of scope, anon subs only; (b) fresh-binding-per-iteration: acceptance probe = the ir3 shape (foreach my $i + push , sub { $i * 10 }) must still yield 10/20/30 with the raw loop var; (c) probe the emission path actually keeps the lambda inline in the let scope on every route (map/grep/sort blocks too).  MEASURE FIRST which routes emit hoisted lambdas.  Bar: corpus-diff + full sweep + bench.

DONE s456af.  Kind-A gate `raw-closure-capture`.  nested-sub-ref is now capture AND event, not capture alone.  MEASURED FIRST as the task asked: every route emits the lambda INLINE in the binding's own let (no hoist), and %expand-foreach-range wraps each iteration in its own (let ((var val)) ...) in the RAW arm too -- so care item (b) holds, `for my $i (1..3) { push @f, sub { $i * 10 } }` gives 10,20,30 with $i raw.  Care item (a) needed no code: the block scan only ever collected ANON subs, because a named sub's block has its own NAME as the previous sibling.  The event oracle is the SHARED _text_gate_tags list (published as Pl::VarAnnotator::text_gate_tags for this caller and #761's) run on the closure BODY with the bare-write gate: text-shaped, so it over-fires, which is the safe direction.  22 probes vs perl identical, incl. the six that must still box (write, \$s, +=, ++, chomp, a writer among readers).  Guard rows 13-18; the stale twin Pl/t/parser2-01.t:167 asserted the removed conservatism and was rewritten.
